ops.title: Lease-free cross-host live-session ranking penalty
ops.description:
The origin-owned cred-sync redesign (Phase 3) deleted the holder/lease machinery, and with it the cross-host live-session ranking penalty that the lease carried (`syncGate.peerLeaseCounts` fed `rankWithReservations` an extra ActiveSessions count for accounts a peer was actively using). Accepted loss for now: scoring re-converges via usage samples within ~one poll (~3 min), since a peer's live session burns quota that the next `/usage` sample reflects.

Build a secretless replacement: publish per-host live session counts into the sync registry (no credentials — just a count keyed by uuid+host, like the old lease but as pure telemetry) and fold peer counts back into `rankWithReservations` as a soft penalty (never an exclusion), so the pool avoids handing a fresh session to an account another Mac is already hammering, without waiting for the usage sample to catch up.

Context: `internal/daemon/server.go` rankWithReservations (penalty removal), `internal/hostsync` registry (where a `sessions` field would live). Prior art: the deleted `syncGate.peerLeaseCounts` in git history (removed commit on branch worktree-cred-sync-origin).

ops.text: Peer live-session counts propagate through the sync registry with NO credential material (secretless — the redesign's core invariant)
rankWithReservations applies the peer count as a soft ranking penalty, never an exclusion (PickFallback still reaches the account)
Sync-disabled and single-host pooling behavior is byte-identical to today (no regression when only one host is in the mesh)
